Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Staff Product Manager, Test & Code Coverage, you'll build product capabilities from initial discovery through launch and adoption. You'll help engineering teams understand why pipelines fail, improve test automation, and use code coverage to make better decisions about software quality and risk.</p> <p>You'll turn a technically complex problem space into a focused strategy, roadmap, and developer experience. Working closely with Engineering and Design, you'll explore how agents can diagnose failures, recommend next steps, and help teams recover safely. The goal isn't to add artificial intelligence (AI) for its own sake. It's to reduce manual work and help developers get back to a safe, shippable state without losing trust or control.</p> <p>At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. You'll contribute to that mission by making testing and coverage insights more useful across the software development lifecycle.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Define and communicate the Test & Code Coverage product vision, strategy, and outcome-focused roadmap, from discovery through a minimum viable product, beta, launch, and continued iteration.</li> <li>Identify customer problems across pipeline failure diagnosis, test automation, test optimization, code coverage, and recovery. Build the case for investment, prioritize foundational and customer-facing work, and reshape or stop initiatives that aren't creating value.</li> <li>Work with Engineering to understand pipeline failures caused by flaky tests, testing gaps, environment issues, configuration problems, and coverage blind spots. Connect code changes, tests, pipeline behavior, historical patterns, and risk to help developers find a diagnosis and an actionable next step.</li> <li>Work directly with customers to understand how they author, maintain, select, prioritize, and debug tests. Connect test selection, test impact analysis, code coverage, and pipeline intelligence to reduce flaky tests, shorten feedback loops, and focus testing effort where it lowers the most risk.</li> <li>Partner with Engineering and Design to prototype agent-driven workflows for failure diagnosis, test authoring and repair, optimization, coverage analysis, and recovery. Make actions reviewable through evidence, confidence, human approval, and safe paths to propose code changes and merge requests. Use AI tools in your own product work to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and accelerate learning.</li> <li>Define and measure outcomes such as time to diagnose, time to recover, failure recurrence, test signal quality, and developer confidence. Validate problems and solutions with customers and learn from production usage.</li> <li>Partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing to connect testing insights with code review, pipelines, and release decisions. Turn customer evidence into clear narratives that support adoption and future investment.</li> <li>Lead through clear written communication, prioritization, and product judgment. Influence senior stakeholders, establish repeatable discovery and measurement practices, and mentor other product managers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex technical products, platforms, or developer workflows at Staff, Senior Staff, Principal, or equivalent scope, including building a new product or capability from initial validation through launch and adoption.</li> <li>Strong product fundamentals in customer discovery, problem framing, prioritization, roadmap development, outcome measurement, and iterative delivery.</li> <li>Technical fluency in one or more relevant areas, such as software testing, test automation, code coverage, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), developer tools, DevOps, developer experience, quality engineering, or software delivery.</li> <li>An understanding of how engineering teams build, test, review, and ship software, and the ability to work with engineers on test architecture, pipeline behavior, code changes, data, integrations, reliability, and scale.</li> <li>Experience diagnosing technical problems and turning complex, noisy signals into clear user experiences and actionable workflows.</li> <li>Experience exploring AI or agent-driven solutions for developer workflows, with the judgment to distinguish useful automation from unsafe or low-confidence actions.</li> <li>Experience using customer conversations to understand problems and inform product decisions, communicating clearly in writing and conversation, and influencing across functions with shared ownership. You can work directly with developers, quality engineers, platform teams, engineering leaders, and executives, and move between strategy and implementation detail.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Our work brings together Product, Engineering, and Design, with input from Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing. We work directly with developers, quality engineers, and engineering leaders to understand their testing practices, validate ideas, and learn from how they use the product.</p> <p>We give Engineering and Design clear customer context and room to shape solutions. Our decisions draw on customer evidence and measurable outcomes, and we revisit approaches that aren't creating value. You'll contribute to how we discover problems, prioritize work, and measure progress, as well as sharing product management practices with other product managers.</p> <p>As part of GitLab's all-remote organization, we collaborate asynchronously across regions. Our work emphasizes transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. You understand how self-serve adoption works in complex B2B products, including the needs of end users, administrators, and buyers, and how product usage can support broader evaluation and expansion.</p> <p> </p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Define and maintain a 12–18-month product strategy for a cross-team part of GitLab’s AI Software Factory, with customer adoption and growth as core outcomes.</li> <li>Own the adoption journey from discovery and onboarding through activation, time-to-first-value, repeat usage, team adoption, retention, and conversion or expansion.</li> <li>Identify friction in the end-user, administrator, and buyer journeys, and prioritize improvements that help customers realize value and broaden adoption.</li> <li>Set outcome measures for product and growth initiatives; use product usage data, customer feedback, and experiments to evaluate impact and adjust direction.</li> <li>Build a steady test-and-learn approach, including clear hypotheses, experiment design, and sharing results and learnings across partner teams.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Product management experience leading complex technical or multi-team products from strategy through delivery and iteration.</li> <li><strong>Required:</strong> Demonstrated success in enterprise B2B PLG or growth, with measurable impact on activation, time-to-value, adoption, retention, conversion, or expansion—including scaling from individual use to team or organization-wide adoption.</li> <li>Hands-on experience using customer research, product analytics, funnel and cohort analysis, and experimentation to identify growth opportunities and measure results.</li> <li>Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle and experience with AI products, developer tools, DevSecOps, or other technical B2B software.</li> <li>Sound technical judgment and a track record of influencing cross-functional teams, resolving tradeoffs, and communicating product decisions clearly in ambiguous environments.</li> </ul> <p>We welcome candidates with different backgrounds and transferable experience. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>This role works across GitLab to connect teams building the future of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You’ll partner closely with the GitLab Duo Agent Platform organization and with product areas that own key parts of the software development workflow. The team’s challenge is to turn work delivered across several groups into one clear, end-to-end experience—and to help more users discover, adopt, and realize value from it through product-led growth.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Staff Product Manager,  RevOps & Finance Systems
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An Overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>We are seeking a Staff Product Manager to serve as an internal PM embedded within this team. This is not a traditional external-facing product role—it is an internal platform product leadership position. You will own the roadmap for our enterprise systems, act as the strategic voice of the business within engineering, and bring senior product craft to a team of Analysts and engineers who build and operate GitLab's revenue infrastructure. </p> <p>This role is ideal for a seasoned product leader who has deep Quote-to-Cash or Finance domain knowledge, thrives at the intersection of business strategy and technical execution, and is energized by mentoring high-performing teams through complex, multi-program environments.</p> <h3><strong>What You’ll Do  </strong></h3> <p><strong>Internal Product Roadmap Ownership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define, own, and maintain the multi-quarter internal product roadmap for QTC and Finance Systems, covering Salesforce CPQ, Zuora Billing, Zuora Revenue, NetSuite, and the CDot metering platform.</li> <li>Translate business strategy from Finance, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Sales into sequenced, prioritized system capabilities with clear outcomes and success metrics.</li> <li>Balance competing program demands—stabilization, net-new capability delivery, and technical debt reduction—with transparent trade-off frameworks.</li> <li>Drive quarterly and annual planning ceremonies, partnering with Engineering Managers and Business Systems Analysts to align capacity with roadmap commitments.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements Translation</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary internal product voice for all QTC and Finance Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Finance, Accounting, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Legal.</li> <li>Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions to translate complex financial and commercial requirements into actionable system specifications.</li> <li>Own the decision layer between "what the business needs" and "what engineering builds," resolving ambiguity with structured frameworks and documented decisions.</li> <li>Navigate cross-functional stakeholder dynamics including SOX compliance, audit controls, and revenue recognition governance (ASC 606/IFRS 15).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team Mentorship & Capability Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as a product craft mentor and senior thought partner for the BSA team, actively upskilling analysts in product thinking, requirements structuring, acceptance criteria definition, and roadmap communication.</li> <li>Model and instill product management best practices—user story writing, prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, MoSCoW), sprint review discipline, and outcome tracking—across the team.</li> <li>Partner with leadership to evolve the operating model of the team from project-execution-focused to product-thinking-led, raising the bar for how ETA delivers business value.</li> <li>Provide structured feedback and growth coaching to BSAs on career development, helping analysts grow toward senior and lead levels.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead product strategy for major multi-quarter programs (e.g., consumption-based billing iterations, CLM/Order Forms, Zuora Product Catalog refactors, ERP optimization) from discovery through go-live.</li> <li>Define and maintain program-level dependency maps across concurrent workstreams, surfacing risks early and driving cross-team resolution.</li> <li>Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release.</li> <li>Support post-launch stabilization and continuous improvement cycles, prioritizing defect resolution and incremental enhancements based on business impact.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Systems Architecture Collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers to evaluate build-vs-buy-vs-configure decisions for new capabilities.</li> <li>Bring informed opinions on QTC platform architecture trade-offs (e.g., billing model design, middleware integration patterns, revenue recognition rule configuration) based on deep domain knowledge.</li> <li>Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce, Zuora, and NetSuite, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></h3> <ul> <li>8+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years in an internal platform PM, enterprise applications PM, or systems product leadership role.</li> <li>Deep domain expertise in Quote-to-Cash systems: Salesforce CPQ, Zuora Billing, Zuora Revenue, and NetSuite ERP are the core stack—hands-on configuration or implementation experience strongly preferred.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders.</li> <li>Strong command of revenue lifecycle processes: opportunity-to-quote, order management, billing and collections, revenue recognition (ASC 606), and financial close.</li> <li>Experience operating in a SOX-controlled environment with an understanding of audit trails, approval workflows, and change management requirements for financial systems.</li> <li>Track record of successfully running complex, multi-program delivery environments with competing priorities and shared engineering resources.</li> <li>Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs—without needing to write code.</li> <li>Experience with consumption-based or usage-based billing models</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>You'll be joining the Revenue Lifecycle & Finance Systems team within GitLab's Enterprise Technology Architecture organization. Our team is responsible for the systems and processes that power GitLab's entire revenue lifecycle—from configure-price-quote through contract execution, billing, revenue recognition, and financial close. </p> <p>We are in an exciting and demanding phase: transitioning GitLab's go-to-market from a pure subscription model toward consumption-based offerings while simultaneously modernizing our core platforms. This role will be central to shaping how that evolution happens—and how the team grows in capability and product maturity alongside it.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. projects, and coordinate with Application Security so that review coverage is comprehensive and correctly prioritised</li> <li>Threat model new and existing systems, and establish the patterns that let teams threat model their own work</li> <li>Work with Security Research on proactive exploration of unknown risks in GitLab's architecture</li> <li>Anticipate emerging security challenges and propose architectural responses before they reach implementation</li> <li>Mentor security engineers across the division, and represent security architecture to engineering audiences</li> </ul> trust boundary analysis</li> <li>Experience securing distributed systems, including service-to-service authentication, secrets handling, and the failure modes of security decisions made across process boundaries</li> <li>Working knowledge of software supply chain security: build and release integrity, artifact provenance, and dependency risk</li> <li>A track record of proactive architecture work — identifying risk before it becomes an incident, and designing something that prevents a class of problem rather than an instance of one</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with engineering leadership and influence technical direction through expertise rather than gatekeeping</li> <li>Experience defining security standards or patterns that teams adopted without being compelled to</li> <li>The ability to operate strategically while remaining hands-on, including reading unfamiliar code, building prototypes, and contributing changes</li> <li>Clear written communication, and the ability to make a security argument to an engineering audience that does not already agree with it</li> <li>A view on how security guidance should be authored and delivered for AI coding tools, not only for humans</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>Security Architects are a part of our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/">Security Platforms and Architecture</a> team, who address complex security challenges facing GitLab and its customers to enable GitLab to be the most secure software factory platform on the market. </ul> <p>What you'll bring</p> <ul> <li>Experience leading complex, cross-functional strategic programs at the executive level and turning ambiguous direction into delivered outcomes without a fully expansion, and adoption motions and how they contribute to ARR.</li> <li>The ability to influence senior stakeholders, including executives, and hold them accountable to commitments without formal authority.</li> <li>Judgment to make high-stakes tactical recommendations under ambiguity, including when data supports changing direction or ending a program.</li> <li>Data fluency to assess program health, diagnose where work is breaking down, and recommend a data-informed next step.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to move between an executive-ready narrative conflict and competing priorities across a broad stakeholder group.</li> </ul> <p>About the team</p> <p>You'll be the first Program Manager supporting CX Executive initiatives and the founding hire in Translate business needs into requirements, validate solutions, and strengthen data quality and operational controls.</li> <li>Simplify and scale the renewal motion through automation, standardized workflows, alerts, playbooks, and self-service insights that reduce manual effort and improve execution consistency.</li> <li>Support renewals planning and capacity management, including segmentation implementation, coverage models, productivity assumptions, capacity modeling, supporting target setting, and scenario planning.</li> <li>Own and mature the Renewal Operations case-management program, including intake, triage, routing, service-level visibility, resolution, and root-cause analysis. Requests may include user migrations, de-duplication, Renewal Manager ownership changes, compensation exceptions, and Salesforce or data issues.</li> <li>Raise the operating standard in your domain by documenting processes, mentoring others on how the renewal motion works, and contributing to broader Revenue Operations initiatives that need the renewals perspective.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in Renewals Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, management consulting, strategy, or a similar analytical and problem-solving role, with ownership of operational improvements and cross-functional initiatives.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with both consumption and subscription renewal motions, including renewal forecasting, retention reporting, and the contractual and process mechanics that govern how renewals close.</li> <li>Strong critical thinking and structured problem-solving skills. You can break down ambiguous problems into clear workstreams and move them forward.</li> <li>Strong quantitative and analytical skills. You're highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets, can build and validate models from scratch, and can translate analysis into clear recommendations and action. Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) or equivalent data-querying tools is preferred, not required.</li> <li>Systems thinking and experience using Salesforce for pipeline and renewals reporting. You understand how changes in one part of the go-to-market motion affect others, including how CRM, subscription or entitlement records, quoting, and billing relate to one another, and you design solutions accordingly.</li> <li>Sound commercial judgment and an understanding of renewal complexity, including co-terming, amendments, expansions, downgrades, price changes, multiyear agreements, auto-renewals, procurement requirements, and approval policies.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional collaboration skills. You build trust with stakeholders at all levels, including field teams and senior leadership, and influence without direct authority.</li> <li>Curiosity, sound judgment, and a bias toward action. You learn new domains and tools quickly, move from insight to implementation, and follow through until improvements are adopted and sustained.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>You'll work within CX Operations, partnering closely with Renewals and Customer Success leadership, Sales, Finance, Revenue Technology, and Revenue Analytics. policy.</li> <li>Maintain mappings between our policies and frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, and NIST CSF, so requirements are written once and reused.</li> </ul> <li><em>Measurement and assurance</em></li> <ul> <li>Define KPIs for policy adherence and report trends to Security leadership.</li> <li>Run targeted internal assessments of adherence and drive remediation to closure.</li> <li>Support audit activities by coordinating evidence, testing, and remediation management.</li> </ul> <li><em>Customer trust</em></li> <ul> <li>Support customer questionnaires and customer meetings, and help turn recurring customer requests into better policies and self-service content.</li> </ul> <li><em>Automation and AI</em></li> <ul> <li>Identify and implement automation and AI-assisted workflows for policy management, evidence collection, control monitoring, and assessment work, in partnership with GRC Engineering.</li> </ul> <li><em>Technical leadership</em></li> <ul> <li>Act as a technical and program leader across Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering, influencing without direct authority.</li> <li>Mentor other team members and help set the direction of the Security Governance roadmap.</li> </ul> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>10+ years in security governance, GRC, or IT risk, with hands-on ownership of a policy and standards lifecycle and measurable outcomes, ideally at a global technology company.</li> <li>Working knowledge of SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, and NIST CSF, including how to put them into practice, not only how to read them</li> <li>Experience creating and maintaining an enterprise Information Security Management System (ISMS), ideally including hands on involvement in ISO 27001 certification or recertification.<span class="screenreader-hidden-offscreen"> </span></li> <li>Understanding of cloud, SaaS, and DevSecOps practices, and the ability to write policy that engineers will follow.</li> <li>A risk-based mindset that balances compliance with real security risk.</li> <li>Demonstrated use of automation or AI to reduce manual GRC work.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication, including translating technical concepts for engineers, executives, auditors, and customers.</li> <li>Experience collaborating with Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering.</li> <li>Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, or similar are highly desirable.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What success looks like</strong></h4> <ul> <li>First 30 days: Assessed the current policy library and exception process, built relationships with key stakeholders, and proposed a prioritized roadmap.</li> <li>First 90 days: Uplift the existing security policy library to align with NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27017/27018/42001, and PCI-DSS.</li> <li>First 120 days: A refreshed review cadence is in place, exception reporting is running, and can demonstrate a measurable improvement in policy adherence.</li> <li>First six months: Develop Policy as Code and collaborate with Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering for implementation into existing workflows.</li> </ul> Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.</p> <p>Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.</p> <p>What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.</li> <li>Own the architecture of the program model (parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis) and of the pipeline that turns source code into findings, and define how both extend to new languages and frameworks</li> <li>Solve technical problems of the highest scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, UX, and partner teams such as Code Security and Composition Analysis</li> <li>Mentor all engineers on the team through code review and pairing, remove blockers to their autonomy, and shepherd the definition and improvement of our internal standards through review</li> <li>Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues</li> <li>Define the overarching architecture and specification documents for the engine, delegate component specifications within them, and drive their implementation by AI agents and engineers working independently through phased plans, small reviewable units of change, and specifications kept in lockstep with the code</li> <li>Build and maintain the harness, agent instructions, and agentic skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy, including separate coding and reviewing agents, rules and tests the coding agents cannot change, independent review panels of agents from different model providers, and performance, API, and dependency gates, with risky changes escalated to human review</li> <li>Stay current with research in program analysis and security, run AI-assisted research and spikes, and turn the findings into prototypes, proposals, and upstream contributions, including responsible disclosure of findings in open source projects</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't</li> <li>Extensive professional experience writing, testing, and reviewing production code in Rust, Go, or a comparable systems language, with depth in at least one. The engine is Rust, the analyzer wrapper is Go, and the monolith integration is Ruby, and we value willingness to work across them.</li> <li>Experience with performance optimization and with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)</li> <li>A deep program analysis and static analysis background, such as parsing and ASTs, intermediate representations (SSA, control-flow and call graphs), taint and data-flow analysis, type inference, incremental and fixpoint computation, or writing detection rules, with the ability to read, evaluate, and apply the research literature</li> <li>Deep application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE)</li> <li>Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems, and to write architecture and design specifications that bring a team to a decision</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous, team-wide problems and shipping them from concept to production with minimal guidance, with specific, regular async updates on progress, blockers, risks, and next steps</li> <li>Experience defining a system's overarching architecture, delegating component specifications to engineers and AI agents, and getting them implemented reliably</li> <li>A track record of mentoring engineers, raising a team's technical bar, and influencing technical direction by achieving consensus with peers and leadership</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Helpful experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration</li> <li>Experience designing guardrails for agent-written code, such as mutation testing, fuzzing, and CI gates the coding agent cannot modify</li> <li>A record of engaging with the research community, such as publications, tool papers, or upstream open source contributions in program analysis or security</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories.</p> <p>We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules & flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. title: Strategic Account Executive, AI - San Francisco
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>Location- San Francisco, California </strong></h3> <h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Strategic Account Executive for the San Francisco region, you'll drive GitLab's enterprise growth by helping some of the area's most influential organizations, including a concentrated focus on leading AI companies, adopt, implement, and expand their use of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You'll focus on enterprise accounts, with particular emphasis on foundation model labs, AI infrastructure providers, and applied AI companies scaling rapidly in the region, guiding customers through complex digital and DevSecOps transformations and driving pipeline generation that translates into measurable Net ARR and long-term expansion. In this role, you'll act as a key connector between customer stakeholders and GitLab's field organization so GitLab is seen as a trusted, long-term partner across the full sales cycle. In your first year, you'll be expected to build a strong enterprise portfolio across your territory, including a meaningful share of AI-native accounts, create repeatable sales motions, and consistently forecast and report on deal progress and account health.</p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Drive strategic growth by leading GitLab's enterprise accounts across San Francisco, with a dedicated focus on AI-native companies, serving as a trusted technology advisor to industry leaders in your territory.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Orchestrate winning sales strategies by bringing together Solutions Architects, Customer Success experts, Sales Development, Channel & Alliances, and other technical specialists to deliver transformative, AI-powered DevSecOps solutions tailored to the unique velocity and scale demands of AI-native engineering organizations.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Shape the future of software development by crafting innovative solutions that align GitLab's platform with customers' long-term vision, compliance needs, and business objectives, including the specific infrastructure, security, and governance challenges AI companies face as they scale model development and deployment.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Build deep, strategic partnerships by mastering your customers' industry landscape, success metrics, and growth trajectories, including a strong point of view on the AI/ML ecosystem, so you can position GitLab as their indispensable technology ally.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Design and execute strategic account plans, including opportunity mapping, stakeholder alignment, and multi-threaded engagement, to expand GitLab usage within new and existing strategic accounts, with particular attention to fast-growing AI companies and their evolving technical buying committees.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Lead end-to-end customer journeys from initial discovery through evaluation, negotiation, and successful implementation, ensuring a consistent, high-quality experience at every stage of the sales cycle.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Champion continuous improvement by contributing to forecasting and pipeline reviews, conducting sophisticated win/loss analyses, and sharing strategic insights, including emerging trends in AI company buying behavior, that refine our go-to-market approach.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Prepare and deliver compelling customer-facing and internal presentations, proposals, and recommendations that clearly communicate value, business outcomes, and the path to long-term partnership with GitLab.</li> <li> </li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Experience driving complex B2B software sales cycles with enterprise customers, ideally in DevSecOps, software development tools, or adjacent SaaS solutions.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Background selling into large, enterprise accounts in San Francisco, United States, with the ability to build trusted C-level and senior stakeholder relationships across business and technical teams.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Familiarity with the AI/ML company landscape, including model providers, AI infrastructure vendors, and applied AI startups, and the ability to speak credibly to engineering and technical leadership about how DevSecOps practices apply to AI-driven development.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Knowledge of San Francisco's enterprise and AI market, including key industries, buying centers, and decision-making dynamics, with the ability to build and nurture a relevant professional network.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Ability to drive new business acquisition and expansion within enterprise accounts through consultative, multi-stakeholder sales motions that lead to sustainable, long-term customer partnerships.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Experience collaborating with channel and strategic partners to generate pipeline, co-sell, and support successful customer adoption.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead account strategy, influence internal and external stakeholders, and remain calm under pressure.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Ability to work in line with GitLab's values, use GitLab and Salesforce in your daily work, and travel as needed while following company travel policies.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Enterprise Sales team is responsible for driving growth, adoption, and long-term value for GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps platform with our largest and most strategic customers. As a Strategic Account Executive focused on San Francisco, you'll be part of a distributed, all-remote team that works asynchronously across regions and partners closely with GitLab's sales engineering, marketing, and customer success teams. We value transparency, collaboration, and a consultative approach, and we support one another through shared account planning, regular deal reviews, and knowledge sharing focused on enterprise customers across the San Francisco region.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong><strong class="textBold">An overview of this role</strong></strong></p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">This is an overnight shift role with working hours of 12:00am - 7:00am EST.</span></h4> <p>As a Support Engineer on our U.S. Government Support Engineering team, you operate at the critical intersection of Support and Engineering, enabling public sector organizations and United States government agencies to run GitLab in some of the most secure and constrained environments in the world. Your work directly supports national security missions, including customers operating within FedRAMP-authorized, air-gapped, and classified or semi-classified environments where traditional troubleshooting approaches are not always possible.</p> <p>In this role, you will engage deeply with GitLab through the command line; analyzing logs, system behavior, and application performance with strong Linux fundamentals and an understanding of how GitLab’s components interact end-to-end. You may partner with Product and Engineering to reproduce and document edge-case defects using sanitized or redacted data, or contribute directly to the product by opening merge requests that resolve customer-impacting issues. Beyond resolving individual cases, you’ll help strengthen GitLab by improving documentation, support workflows, and institutional knowledge, ensuring that lessons learned in highly regulated environments benefit the broader platform; all while working in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment built on trust, autonomy, and shared ownership.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/strace-parser"><u><span class="textUnderline">A tool to quickly analyze strace output</span></u></a></li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos"><u><span class="textUnderline">A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting</span></u></a></li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/chatops/"><u><span class="textUnderline">A functionality to ChatOps to make it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</span></u></a></li> </ul> <h2><strong><strong class="textBold">What you’ll do</strong></strong></h2> <ul> <li value="1">Collaborate closely with public sector customers, including U.S. government agencies, the Department of War, and Intelligence Community organizations, to diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve complex issues in GitLab deployments operating under strict security, compliance, and operational constraints.</li> <li value="2">Perform deep, hands-on technical investigations using Linux command-line tooling and GitLab internals to analyze logs, system performance, and application behavior, often with limited telemetry or incomplete datasets. You will trace issues across infrastructure, application, and code paths to identify root causes, recommend mitigations, and drive durable fixes; frequently partnering with GitLab Product, Development, and Infrastructure teams to ensure outcomes that meet both mission and platform reliability requirements.</li> <li value="3">Create and update clear, reusable documentation and support content based on real customer interactions to improve self-service and reduce repeated issues.</li> <li value="4">Participate in regular<a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w"> <u><span class="textUnderline">pairing sessions</span></u></a> with other Support Engineers and act as a<a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart"> <u><span class="textUnderline">stable counterpart</span></u></a> to cross-functional teams to share knowledge and improve support processes.</li> <li value="5">Contribute to building and refining internal support tools and workflows, including automation and troubleshooting utilities, to make diagnosing and resolving issues more efficient.</li> <li value="6">Participate in weekday and weekend on-call rotations, providing timely emergency support for self-managed customers operating in restricted and compliance-focused environments.</li> <li value="7">Support the growth of the team by reviewing applications and assessments, and participating in interviews and hiring decision discussions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong><strong class="textBold">What you’ll bring</strong></strong></h2> <ul> <li value="1">Due to government security requirements, you must be a United States Citizen (defined as any individual who is a citizen of the United States by law, birth, or naturalization) to be eligible for this position</li> <li value="2">Experience managing customer-facing cases across the full support lifecycle, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge, with the ability to troubleshoot performance and configuration issues in complex environments</li> <li value="4">Familiarity with AI/LLM-powered developer tooling and gateway architectures (for example GitLab Duo, AI gateway configurations, or similar model-serving/proxy layers), including how they're deployed and troubleshot in self-managed or air-gapped environments</li> <li value="5">Ability to use scripting languages (preferably Ruby or Bash) and work within model-view-controller frameworks (preferably Ruby on Rails) to investigate and resolve issues</li> <li value="6">Practical experience with Git and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflows</li> <li value="7">Skill in creating and maintaining clear, accurate support content and technical documentation</li> <li value="8">Ability to explain complex technical topics in a clear, empathetic way to customers and coworkers with varying technical backgrounds</li> <li value="9">Familiarity with DevOps practices and container-orchestration technologies such as OpenShift and Kubernetes</li> <li value="10">Understanding of common information security and compliance concepts and controls (for example DISA STIG and SELinux), and eligibility to work on United States federal customer environments as required for this role</li> </ul> <h2><strong><strong class="textBold">About the team</strong></strong></h2> <p>At GitLab Federal, LLC, the U.S. Government Support Engineering team partners with public sector organizations and United States government agencies to support GitLab in highly secure, mission-critical environments. Our work directly enables national security outcomes, supporting customers across the Intelligence Community, Department of War, and other federal, state, and local government entities operating within regulated and restricted boundaries.</p> <p>We are embedded within Support Engineering and work closely with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to solve complex, high-impact technical challenges. Our team frequently dives into code, logs, and architectural behavior to understand not just what is failing, but why; especially in environments with sanitized data, limited visibility, and strict compliance controls such as FedRAMP. We collaborate asynchronously across time zones and through structured pairing and discussion to share knowledge, strengthen solutions, and continuously improve how GitLab supports secure, air-gapped, and regulated deployments, while upholding GitLab's standards for rigor, transparency, and technical excellence.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. value="6">Use content, channel, candidate feedback, and funnel metrics to improve performance and communicate impact.</li> <li value="7">Collaborate across GitLab to ensure content is accurate, iteration and thoughtful use of technology and artificial intelligence tools.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li value="1">Experience in talent brand, employer brand, experiences.</li> <li value="3">Strong storytelling, writing, editing, and editorial judgment across multiple channels.</li> <li value="4">Experience planning and delivering campaigns or programs with values and remote working practices, and applicable work authorization.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The GitLab Talent Brand team helps candidates understand what it means to title: Tech Operations Specialist
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>The Tech Operations Specialist keeps the field organization's AI tooling running smoothly day to day. You will maintain a clear inventory of AI tools in use across the field, manage an index of use cases and field needs, track adoption and utilization, manage access requests, and keep the underlying data feeding these tools clean and well-organized. This is a detail-oriented, execution-focused role for someone who enjoys bringing order to a fast-moving tool landscape and wants to build a foundation in Tech operations.</p> <p>This role reports to the Vice President, Enablement & AI.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li><strong>Tool Inventory & Consolidation:</strong> Maintain an up-to-date inventory of all AI tools used across the field org, identify overlap or redundancy, and support consolidation efforts to reduce tool sprawl.</li> <li><strong>Tool Adoption & Use Case Index: </strong>Formalize a library of field-adopted and -requested use cases for our AI tools, in coordination with the AI Transformation Owner, CRO.</li> <li><strong>Utilization & Tracking:</strong> Monitor usage of AI tools across teams, build simple reporting to track adoption trends, and flag underutilized or underperforming tools to stakeholders.</li> <li><strong>Comms & Enablement: </strong>draft internal announcements for tool rollouts and create micro-enablement programs to engage the field in AI tools.</li> <li><strong>Tool Access Requests/Management:</strong> Own the intake and processing of access requests for AI tools, ensuring provisioning is timely, accurate, and aligned with licensing and approval requirements.</li> <li><strong>AI Data Management:</strong> Support the organization, quality, and hygiene of data used by or generated from AI tools, working with relevant teams to keep gDrive/datasets accurate and properly maintained.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Early-Mid Level Experience:</strong> Some experience in enablement, sales/business operations, IT operations, or a similar coordination-heavy function; Act as an advocate for AI Adoption and best practices in the field.</li> <li><strong>Process-Minded:</strong> Comfortable following and improving structured processes (intake forms, access workflows, tracking dashboards) rather than needing to build strategy from scratch.</li> <li><strong>Collaborative:</strong> Able to work with enablement, IT, and field stakeholders to gather requirements and resolve access or data issues efficiently.</li> <li><strong>Data Comfort:</strong> Basic comfort working with spreadsheets, dashboards, or simple data tools to track utilization and maintain data quality.</li> <li><strong>GitLab Values Alignment:</strong> Ability to work in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, leaning heavily on transparency and collaboration as defined in the GitLab Handbook.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Enablement & AI function is part of the CRO organization. Enablement is instrumental in helping GitLab grow at a more accelerated pace and achieve our ambitious revenue targets. The enablement organization comprises enablement leads serving the CRO business functions, a centralized content group, AI tech resources, and an operations team.</p> <p> </p> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/" target="_blank">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/paid-time-off/" target="_blank">Flexible Paid Time Off</a> </li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/erg-guide/#:~:text=Definition%20of%20the%20TMRG%20%2D%20Team%20Member%20Resource%20Groups,-TMRGs%20are%20voluntary&text=The%20purpose%20for%20this%20type,developing%20the%20sense%20of%20belonging." target="_blank">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/" target="_blank">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/" target="_blank">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave" target="_blank">Parental leave</a> </li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/expenses/#equipment" target="_blank">Home office</a> support</li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. title: Senior / Staff Security Engineer
description: At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires. Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 30,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship. At Linear, we are committed to quality. Security is an essential part of that quality — not a layer that we add later, but something we build in from the start. We have a foundational security program we're proud of but, as Linear evolves our product and scales into enterprise, there's meaningful work ahead: staying ahead of vulnerabilities as our attack surface grows, responding fast and cleanly when incidents happen, and hardening our product and infrastructure. As Security Engineer at Linear, you'll be operating in a high-autonomy role with real scope, doing hands-on security work across the product and infrastructure we build. Location & work mode Linear is a remote-first company. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel. What you’ll do Depending on your experience / skillset and our broader priorities, you could: - Operate, automate, and extend vulnerability management end-to-end: triage, prioritize, and drive remediation across product, infrastructure, and dependencies, and keep the program’s SLAs meaningful rather than theoretical - Run our bug bounty program: triage incoming reports, validate severity, work with engineering on fixes, and keep researcher relationships professional and responsive - Lead product security testing: threat model new features (including AI/agent-facing surfaces), review designs and code for security-relevant risk, and do hands-on testing (manual and tool-assisted) rather than relying solely on scanners - Be a primary responder for security incidents: lead investigation and containment, drive postmortems, and turn lessons into concrete hardening work - Own meaningful chunks of our cloud/infra security posture on GCP/k8s/Postgres: harden configurations, close gaps surfaced by audits or scanning, and partner with infra engineering on secure defaults - Build and maintain security tooling and automation, including using AI/LLM tooling to speed up triage, code review, and repetitive investigation work, so the program scales without linear headcount growth - Partner with the GRC/Trust function: feed real findings into the risk register and control evidence, and help make sure compliance requirements reflect actual engineering practice What we’re looking for - A generalist, senior-level security engineer (5+ years across security engineering, with real depth in at least two of: vulnerability management, product/appsec testing, incident response, and cloud security). We need breadth, rather than a narrow specialist in any one of these. - Hands-on and technical: you can read and reason about code (we use a lot of TypeScript), you’re comfortable in cloud environments (GCP a plus), and you can go deep on a finding rather than just filing a ticket for someone else to fix. You’re comfortable using AI coding/security tools as force multipliers (Linear Agent, Claude, Codex, etc). - Calm under pressure: you can lead an incident from first alert through postmortem without needing to be told what to do next - A builder: you’d rather write a script or ship a tool than repeat a manual process a third time - A pragmatic risk-reducer: you optimize for actually reducing risk, not for checking a box or maximizing findings count - Autonomy-oriented: comfortable setting your own priorities, working with significant independence, and knowing when to escalate - A clear communicator: able to explain a technical finding to a non-technical stakeholder and write it up so it’s actually actionable Our tech This is a hands-on security engineering role. You'll be running tools, reading/writing code, building detections, working in our cloud environment, and partnering closely with the engineers who build our product. Our stack is fronted by Cloudflare and runs on Google Cloud with k8s, Postgres, and Node. For day-to-day work, we use: - Linear, GitHub, Slack, and Google Workspace for collaboration - Claude and ChatGPT for general & engineering-specific AI tasks - Vanta for compliance automation and evidence collection Our security-specific tooling includes: - GitHub Advanced Security - RunReveal - SentinelOne What we offer We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. title: SVP, Partners
description: Join Vonage and help us innovate cloud communications for businesses worldwide! Why this role matters: Vonage is doubling down on partnerships as a primary growth engine — and this is the role that owns it all. As SVP, Partners, you will be the single executive accountable for Vonage's entire global partner strategy across both BU API and BU Apps, spanning all nine partner pillars: Hyperscalers, Independent Software Vendors, Value Added Resellers, BU Partners, Developer Platforms, System Integrators, Communications Service Providers, TSD Channel Partners, and Alliance Partners. This is an Executive level leadership role with full P&L-adjacent accountability for the total partner ecosystem — from sell-to and sell-through motions to 360 strategic relationship management. You will set the vision, build the operating model, and lead a team of senior partner leaders to turn Vonage's partner network into a material, measurable revenue channel. If you are an operator and a visionary who can work at board level and roll up your sleeves when it counts, this role is for you. Your key responsibilities: Total Partner Strategy Own and execute Vonage's global partner strategy across all business & product areas — the first unified partner leadership role across our core CPaaS, UCaaS, CCaaS, or adjacent cloud technology sector Familiarity with Salesforce, ServiceNow, or hyperscaler (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure) partner ecosystems and co-sell programmes
